mechanics_product_scope.primary_contract: 3D position and 3D orientation on explicitly declared grip anchor with existing positional drag and fixed world-space contact constraints
mechanics_product_scope.objective: 9-row chordal Frobenius rotation-basis difference combined with 3-row world grip-point position, standard IK drag and pin residuals
mechanics_product_scope.analytic_jacobian: world angular axis cross each rotated local-basis column for orientation; world angular axis cross (world grip point - pivot) for grip-position derivative
mechanics_product_scope.final_court: independent SO(3) angle geodesic tolerance and explicit world-frame positional error; solver success alone insufficient
mechanics_product_scope.authority: declared canonical rig attachment local_P and optional explicitly present metadata.local_basis

verified_cases: simultaneously drag distal A2 tip, orient attached A1 grip to target world 3x3 rotation and preserve B2 planted world contact
full grip-frame world point + orientation 6D objective, independent analytic Jacobian checked vs centered finite differences
contradictory target world position or orientation explicitly FAILs original full constraint
missing local grip orientation cannot be used as orientation target; position-only declared grip can still be solved without inventing orientation
invalid/unknown world grip targets, nonorthonormal 3x3 basis and unsupported mode rejected
live runtime defaults to evaluator and requires explicit opted-in analytic multigoal solver
five-frame sequence drives time-varying attachment world position and world orientation while preserving pinned contact and warm start
competing static and keyed frame target authority rejected
limits: Synthetic explicitly authored grip fixture only; no independent source→canonical correspondence court or unseen subjects
3D grip rotation is explicit metadata rather than an automatic inferred contact frame
one attached grip on a 5-joint dual-chain case; not arbitrary orientation-heavy complex morphology
9-row chordal optimization is exact derivative of the chosen objective but not a guarantee of global nonlinear convergence
local 6D attachment constraints use numerical tolerances, not hard force-contact or friction constraints
per-frame target maps are transient runtime data; no canonical training authority
